version_code.record: OpenHarmony docs: versionCode may be any positive integer but must increase with every release. Deriving it from package.version keeps it from drifting from versionName; the generator refuses a version whose segments exceed max_segment instead of truncating it silently.

start_window_icon.note: No platform document states a required pixel size for the start window icon resource; 512 px is the derived large master size, and its appearance is a verification item. Sizes seen in DevEco generated samples (144 px) are observations of another project, not a specification.

install.note: AppScope resources are merged into the module at build time and override same-named module files, so the layered icon is declared once in AppScope. The file names are DevEco conventions rather than platform requirements - a resource name is free as long as the $media reference matches the file - and they are kept conventional here so a generated project can be compared directly.

theme.note: The start window background is a $color resource, so the dark resource qualifier changes it without a second manifest; the committed values are the proposed surfaces from resources/host/icons/theme.json and are replaced by the host theme work at T05.02/T24.02.

host_requirement.arkts_shell: entry/src/main/ets (EntryAbility, the page and the native bridge) is now part of this scaffold. It forwards to the pinned revision's C ABI; it is not a second UI implementation.
host_requirement.native_library: librust_widgets.so built with the xcomponent feature, placed under entry/libs/arm64-v8a; CMake refuses to configure without it rather than linking a bridge-less module.
host_requirement.remaining_blocker: the identity is recorded (T00.04/T25.02), so the build profile's minimum OS is substituted; what remains is signing (configured per release machine, never committed) and a 2in1 device to install the signed HAP on before any support claim.
host_requirement.note: The candidate Rust triple is a target this machine has installed through rustup. OpenHarmony documents Rust for system level builds and C ABI interop, while the application side native kit is documented for C/C++ and Node-API; no document describes a Rust windowing or event loop path. Whether the pinned GUI stack (winit/wgpu) can be hosted in an OpenHarmony native module on the 2in1 form factor is therefore UNVERIFIED and needs a spike before any support claim.

distribution.note: The HarmonyOS form is the .hap bundle. AppGallery release and internal distribution differ only in the signing profile and the store metadata, which follow T25.02; no credential or store identity is stored in this repository.

verification_required: layered foreground and background reach the launcher on a 2in1 device
start window shows the derived icon and the surface colour in light and dark
the application label resolves from the string resource in the packaged build
bundle identity matches the installed application in the system application list
a clean machine installs the packaged bundle with no development tree and no network
